learning_outcomes.text: Basic knowledge about the use and programming of computers, operating systems, databases and computer programs with application in engineering.
Ability to understand and apply the principles of basic knowledge of general chemistry, organic and inorganic chemistry and their applications in engineering.
Spatial vision capability and knowledge of graphical representation techniques, both by traditional methods of metric geometry and descriptive geometry, and by computer-aided design applications.

syllabus_topics: Introduction. Mechanisms of heat transfer: conduction, convection, and radiation. Temperature and its measurement.

Heat transfer by conduction. Fourier's Law. Thermal conductivity. Heat conduction in solids: one-dimensional and multi-dimensional. Solution of the energy conservation equation in steady and unsteady state. Application of the finite increment method.

Heat transfer by convection. Basic equation of heat transfer by convection. Natural and forced convection. Determination of individual heat transfer coefficients in internal and external flow. Phase change: boiling and condensation.

Heat transfer by radiation. Basic principles of thermal radiation. Basic equation of heat transfer by radiation. Black and gray body. Kirchhoff's Law. View factors. Thermal radiation exchange between surfaces.

Heat exchanger design. Concept of heat exchanger. Types of exchangers. Calculation of the overall heat transfer coefficient. Design equation. LMTD and NUT methods. Incorporation of fins into exchangers: fin effectiveness.
Introduction to energy resources. Current energy landscape. Impact of energy consumption. European directives on energy consumption.

Non-renewable resources. Use of fossil fuels in transport and thermal power plants. Characteristics of fossil fuels. Pollutant emissions from fossil fuels. Fundamentals of nuclear energy: types of nuclear reactors. Radioactive waste.
Renewable resources. Low-temperature solar energy, concentrated solar power, and photovoltaic energy. Wind energy.

assessment_methods.method: Resolution of practical cases related to the course
In-class resolution of problems and practical cases during the course
Laboratory practices and subsequent submission of a report

assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as the weighted average of the assessment activity grades, provided a minimum grade of 5 is achieved for each component. If one or more activities do not meet the minimum grade of 5, the final course grade cannot exceed 4. Students who do not pass in the ordinary call, or did not attend, may take a resit (extraordinary call) only for the re-evaluable activities that were not passed. Laboratory practices are mandatory and not re-evaluable in the extraordinary call. The final grade calculation method remains the same for the extraordinary call.
